0.headline: Anthropic IPO shutout sends Asia's investors into proxy bets
0.heading: Anthropic IPO shutout sends Asia's investors into proxy bets
0.intro: The AI firm is set for an equity offering that may value the company at around $1.5 trillion. While Japan and Australia are included in the international portion of the IPO, access will likely be difficult given high demand and various restrictions.
0.body:
For much of Asia, getting a piece of Anthropic’s blockbuster initial public offering may prove nearly impossible. That’s pushing investors toward a collection of proxies, from the Claude maker’s listed shareholders to crypto derivatives and semiconductor stocks.

The AI firm is set for an equity offering that may value the company at around $1.5 trillion. While Japan and Australia are included in the international portion of the IPO, access will likely be difficult given high demand and various restrictions.

The hunt for indirect exposure is taking investors in several directions. Some are looking to companies with stakes in Anthropic or futures products tied to its valuation, while others are betting on chipmakers and hardware suppliers that could benefit from the AI spending the IPO will help fund.

“It will spill over to chip names,” said Hui Ling Loh, managing director at ACG Management Pte. “Such proxies could be effective way to cover Anthropic as many regional and retail investors are inevitably sidelined in Asia.”

The biggest Anthropic bet in Asia runs through the region’s chip industry. Anthropic’s roughly $800 billion compute buildout points to benefits for leading foundry Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. as well as memory makers like SK Hynix Inc. and Samsung Electronics Co.

The IPO filing highlights Anthropic’s dependence on advanced chips manufactured by TSMC, warning that supply constraints at the Taiwanese supplier are a key concern. SK Hynix and Samsung are also identified in the prospectus as major producers of high-bandwidth memory used in AI computing.

Less obvious trades include SK Telecom Co., whose early investment in Anthropic has grown into a multibillion-dollar holding. The Korean mobile firm also maintains a commercial partnership with the US AI developer.

Commonwealth Bank of Australia offers another route, having purchased a stake in Anthropic more than a year ago. Australia’s biggest lender put the value of its holding at more than $1 billion as of the end of June.

NEC Corp. provides a different kind of connection, having become Anthropic’s first Japan-based global partner in April. It has since joined the AI developer and eight Japanese financial institutions in initiatives to develop AI applications for the financial industry.

NEC shares are up 45% from their June low, while CBA’s stock has risen 8% so far this month. SK Telecom shares have climbed 9% over the past two session, though they’re still well off their June peak.

To be sure, it remains to be seen how the market will receive the giant Nasdaq listing, given the wave of recent concerns over funding for costly AI projects and whether they will ever pay off. Moreover, investing in tangential plays introduces risks from unrelated industries as well.

“People are probably better off sticking with Anthropic’s suppliers,” said Vey-Sern Ling, a managing director at Union Bancaire Privee. “It is a hyped-up IPO of a loss-making company with a very uncertain path to profitability, subject to immense competitive pressures and developmental bottlenecks at the same time.”

Beyond direct equity ownership, cryptocurrency exchanges and online trading platforms are already trading bets on Anthropic. In May, OKX introduced Anthropic-linked perpetual futures that carry no expiry date, followed by similar products from Binance in June.

On Hyperliquid’s EntropyIO venue, Anthropic-linked perpetual futures implied a valuation of about $1.88 trillion. Platforms including PU Prime have introduced contracts-for-difference products that allow traders to speculate on price changes without holding the underlying asset.

1.headline: Jio Platforms joins $100 billion IPO valuation club, only fourth ever after Meta, Alibaba, SpaceX
1.heading: Jio Platforms joins $100 billion IPO valuation club, only fourth ever after Meta, Alibaba, SpaceX
1.intro: Jio Platforms has become only the fourth company ever, after Meta, Alibaba and SpaceX, to enter the $100 billion IPO valuation club. Jio Platforms' shares listed at a 21.4 percent premium, taking the company's market capitalisation of Rs 12.6 lakh crore.
1.body:
Jio Platforms has joined a select group of founder-led businesses, including Meta, Alibaba and SpaceX, to achieve an equity valuation exceeding $100 billion at the time of their initial public offering (IPO). The milestone comes as Jio Platforms made a blockbuster stock market debut on Wednesday, October 28, becoming India's second most valuable listed company.

Jio Platforms shares listed at Rs 1,358 apiece on the stock exchanges, a premium of 21.4 percent over the IPO issue price of Rs 1,119. The listing pushed the company's market capitalisation to Rs 12.6 lakh crore, placing it behind only parent Reliance Industries in India's market capitalisation rankings.

At its IPO offer price, Reliance Industries’ arm Jio Platforms was valued at approximately Rs 10.3 lakh crore, or around $108 billion, putting it alongside Meta, Alibaba and SpaceX in the group of founder-led businesses valued at more than $100 billion around the time of their public market debut.

	Jio Platforms Share Price Live Updates

Jio overtakes Bharti Airtel in market capitalisation
The strong listing also propelled Jio Platforms past Bharti Airtel to become India's most valuable telecom company by market capitalisation. The debut further strengthened Reliance Industries' position, making the Reliance Group India's most valuable conglomerate by aggregate listed market capitalisation.

For investors allotted the minimum lot of 23 shares under the shareholder category, the listing price translated into a gain of Rs 5,497 over the IPO allotment price. The listing ceremony at the National Stock Exchange (NSE) was attended by members of the Ambani family, who marked the occasion with a ceremonial gong strike.
Jio IPO attracts record investor demand
Jio Platforms' Rs 30,213-crore IPO attracted overwhelming demand despite volatility in global equity markets and selling pressure in Indian equities. The issue was subscribed more than 22 times, with combined demand across the public offering and anchor investor placement exceeding Rs 7.4 lakh crore. The public issue was fully subscribed within 95 minutes of opening, while the total number of applications exceeded 1.3 crore.

	Share Markets Live Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty Today

The IPO also marked another major milestone in Jio's capital-raising journey, following its approximately $20 billion private-market fundraise from 13 strategic and private equity investors in 2020. That fundraising had brought major global investors into Jio Platforms, including Meta and Google's parent Alphabet.
From telecom disruptor to listed technology giant
Jio Platforms' public market debut comes a decade after Reliance Jio entered India's telecom industry and expanded access to affordable mobile data. The company now serves more than 540 million customers, according to Managing Director Akash Ambani.

At the listing ceremony, Ambani outlined plans to expand Jio's digital services beyond telecom connectivity into artificial intelligence, cloud computing, connected devices and space-based connectivity.

The company is also exploring international opportunities to monetise its proprietary telecom technology through partnerships with overseas operators.

2.headline: SFC Environmental Technologies IPO booked 16% so far on Day 2; retail investors lead demand
2.heading: SFC Environmental Technologies IPO booked 16% so far on Day 2; retail investors lead demand
2.intro: The initial public offering (IPO) of SFC Environmental Technologies saw subdued demand on the second day of bidding, with the issue receiving 16 percent subscription by 11:42 am on October 28, as per NSE data.
2.body:
The initial public offering (IPO) of SFC Environmental Technologies saw subdued demand on the second day of bidding, with the issue receiving 16 percent subscription by 11:42 am on October 28, as per NSE data.

The Rs 667.5 crore IPO recorded bids for 22,11,660 shares against 1,41,59,744 shares on offer. Retail investors led the demand with 24 percent subscription, followed by non-institutional investors with 18 percent subscription.

In the grey market, SFC Environmental Technologies shares were commanding a grey market premium of 5 percent on the morning of October 28, as per InvestorGain.

Read Also: M K Sons Fine Jewels IPO subscribed 11% so far on Day 1; check latest GMP

The grey market premium is an unofficial indicator of investor sentiment towards a public issue before its listing. However, it does not guarantee listing gains, and the premium can fluctuate depending on market conditions and investor demand.

The company has fixed the IPO price band at Rs 313–330 per share. At the upper end of the price band, SFC Environmental Technologies is valued at Rs 3,232.5 crore.

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of Rs 150 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 1.56 crore equity shares worth Rs 517.5 crore. While the proceeds from the fresh issue will go to the company, the OFS component will allow existing shareholders, including promoters, to sell their shares.

Investors can bid for a minimum of 45 equity shares and in multiples of 45 shares thereafter.

At the upper end of the price band of Rs 330 per share, the minimum investment for retail investors will be Rs 14,850. The maximum investment for a retail investor under the individual retail category will be Rs 1,93,050, equivalent to 585 shares.

The company's shares are expected to list on the stock exchanges on November 3.

Check IPO News Here

The company posted a profit of Rs 1.5 crore in the first quarter of FY27, compared with a loss of Rs 1.3 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.

Revenue nearly doubled to Rs 133.9 crore in the quarter ended June 2026, from Rs 67.8 crore in the year-ago period.

The company plans to use Rs 42.2 crore from the net proceeds of the fresh issue to repay debt and Rs 74.9 crore to meet working capital requirements. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

Incorporated in 2005, SFC Environmental Technologies provides engineering solutions across wastewater treatment, wastewater recycling and reuse, and solid waste treatment.
